title: Scalable long-distance quantum fan-out gates with reduced resource overhead
abstract: Scalable long-distance quantum gates are essential for distributed quantum computation and scalable quantum networks. We propose an efficient scheme for implementing an $n$-qubit fan-out gate $C^n$ (also known as a controlled-NOT-$\cdots$-NOT gate) across spatially separated parties. Our protocol requires only a pre-shared $n$-qubit Greenberger-Horne-Zeilinger state, $n$ local controlled-NOT (CNOT) gates, and feed-forward operations, thereby reducing both the CNOT and Hadamard gate counts by $(n-2)$ when compared with the standard decomposition-based approach. We further develop two optical architectures to implement the heralded and post-selected $n$-photon fan-out gates, respectively. These schemes require fewer single photons resources and achieve higher success probabilities than their decomposition-based counterparts, representing significant improvements. The results indicate that our approach is experimentally feasible and pave the way toward practical long-distance quantum computation.
summary: This paper presents an efficient protocol for implementing long-distance quantum fan-out gates ($C_n$) essential for quantum networks. By leveraging pre-shared GHZ states, the authors significantly reduce the required gate count compared to conventional methods. They further demonstrate the feasibility of these protocols using advanced linear optical architectures for photonic quantum computation.
main_problem: The paper addresses the critical need for scalable, long-distance quantum fan-out gates ($C_n$) necessary for distributed quantum computation and quantum networks.
main_result: The proposed scheme significantly reduces the required number of CNOT and Hadamard gates compared to standard decomposition methods, and the developed optical architectures achieve higher success probabilities.
method: The authors propose a protocol utilizing a pre-shared $n$-qubit Greenberger-Horne-Zeilinger (GHZ) state combined with local CNOT gates and classical feed-forward operations.
model_or_system: The work is modeled abstractly using qubits and then physically realized using linear optics, where qubits are encoded in the polarization states of single photons.
key_observables: Gate counts (CNOT, Hadamard), success probabilities, and quantum circuit diagrams for $C_n$ gates.
important_parameters: Gate counts reduction factor of $(n-2)$, photon survival efficiency ($\eta_s$), and detection efficiencies ($\eta_d$).
main_assumptions: The feasibility relies on the ability to generate and utilize high-fidelity $n$-qubit GHZ states and the performance of linear optical components.
figures_summary: Figures illustrate the quantum circuits for the standard decomposition-based $C_n$ gate and the proposed GHZ-state-based scheme, including schematics for the heralded optical implementation using PBSs.
paper_structure: The paper progresses from defining the problem of scalable $C_n$ gates, detailing the abstract protocol using GHZ states, and finally presenting two specific, highly optimized optical architectures (heralded and post-selected) for photonic implementation.
why_interesting: This work directly tackles the resource overhead challenge in quantum networking by providing resource-efficient gate implementations, which is crucial for scaling up any quantum computation platform.
